author: OpenAxolotl maintainer (uploaded 2026-09-06)
tool: trimesh (https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh), mesh built by an AI-written Python script; version not recorded in the glTF header. Refined headless in Blender 4.0.2 via tools/refine_model.py: 85 parts merged into one mesh per role (skin, eye, gleam, gill, detail), named materials, smooth normals at 60 degrees. Rigged headless in Blender 4.0.2 via tools/rig_model.py: a 12-bone skeleton (root, spine, head, two gills, four legs, three tail segments), weights computed by inverse-square distance to the two nearest bones with the eye and its highlight bound whole to the head, and six animation clips (idle, waddle, swim, hop, fall, hurt). Neither step alters geometry; the triangle count is unchanged throughout.
prompt: Original prompt not recorded at upload. The script assembles a segmented, vertex-coloured axolotl (85 parts, 13,152 triangles, head toward -Z) and exports it as glTF 2.0 binary. The upload carried no rig and no animations; both were added later by the Blender pipeline described above.
